result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Answer B says the existing setup is sound and names specific strengths: the reading size, the leading and the measure. It keeps nearly all values and makes small changes, each with a reason. Answer A rewrites a lot of the stylesheet: bigger body text and headings, color changes, a new paragraph-indent scheme and an optional drop cap. It never acknowledges what already worked, and it leans toward enlarging things and adding decoration. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Answer A says the base setup is sound, names several things that work, and makes a few small, explained edits. Two of those edits are debatable: it changes the h2 spacing and kicker size instead of keeping them, and it changes the blockquote color slightly. Answer B rewrites most of the stylesheet. It enlarges the body and headings, changes colors, swaps paragraph gaps for indents and adds a decorative drop cap, which is the over-editing the rubric warns against.
